title: Agentic protocol
description: Schema for a protocol.json — the data declaration the generic engine interprets. Authoring/editor aid: it is intentionally STRICTER than the engine (which ignores unknown keys) so it catches typos. See docs/PROTOCOL-DSL.md for the field reference.

_note.description: Free-text annotation ignored by the engine (JSON has no comments). Allowed on any object in a protocol.

name.description: Protocol id. Becomes the state-path prefix <name>/<instance-key>.yaml. Unique per protocols directory.

version.description: Protocol version (informational; not enforced by the engine).

min_engine_version.description: Lowest engine version this protocol requires. The dist installer refuses to install onto an older engine.

max_depth.description: Static nesting-depth cap for the protocol tree (default 5). The engine rejects a protocol whose deepest leaf path exceeds this.

phase_labels.description: Optional overrides for the PR labels of terminal/structural phases (e.g. setup, done, failed, blocked).

triggers.description: Event -> command entry points. The router scans every protocol's triggers to select one at runtime.

states.description: The protocol's top-level sequence of nodes (the root is a sequence).

_note.description: Free-text annotation; ignored by the engine.

on.description: GitHub event name, e.g. issue_comment or pull_request.

comment_prefix.description: For issue_comment: match comments starting with this prefix (e.g. /review). Also names the command's reply prefix (e.g. /answer).

actions.description: For pull_request: only fire on these actions (e.g. ["opened"]). Empty/omitted matches any.

target.description: For issue_comment: whether this trigger fires on a comment on a PR (default) or on a plain issue. Plain-issue protocols (e.g. impl-feature-auto, keyed issue-<N>) set "issue".

check.description: A deterministic check over the agent's evidence. ABI: <check> <evidence.json> <diff.txt> <changed-files.txt> -> one JSON {check,pass,feedback}, always exit 0.

_note.description: Free-text annotation; ignored by the engine.

run.description: Check id. Resolved to checks/<run> or checks/<run>.* in the protocol dir (extension-agnostic) unless 'exec' is given.

exec.description: Explicit path (relative to the protocol dir) to the check executable, overriding the checks/<run> lookup.

on_fail.description: Severity when this check fails. iterate (default) drives the retry loop; block stops the conclusion without iterating; advisory is recorded only.

input.description: Materialize an earlier node's evidence (or a question node's answers) as inputs/<as>.json for this node's agent. Exactly one of 'from' or 'from_fork' must be set.

_note.description: Free-text annotation; ignored by the engine.

from.description: Source node id (a sibling sub-state, a fork branch, or a phase).

from_fork.description: code: id of a fork whose legs (per the manifest) are collected — one row per leg with its terminal state + persisted evidence — into inputs/<as>.json.

as.description: Alias — the basename under inputs/ the source is materialized as.

node.description: One node in a sequence. The fields you may set depend on 'kind'.

_note.description: Free-text annotation; ignored by the engine.

id.description: Node id, unique within its enclosing sequence.

kind.description: What this node does. The DSL tracks BPMN 2.0 — each kind maps to a BPMN construct: agent = Service Task (performed by an LLM); code = Script Task (a deterministic hook); choice = Exclusive Gateway (XOR: exactly one outgoing path, picked from an earlier node's evidence); fork = Parallel Gateway (diverging); join = Parallel Gateway (converging); approval = User Task (a human decides: /approve, /request-changes, /reject); question = User Task (a human supplies data via /answer); sequence = Embedded Subprocess (a group of steps entered as one unit).

on.description: choice: which value decides the route. `from` names an earlier node whose evidence is read; `path` is a simple $.dotted JSONPath into it (same restricted syntax as expand.id_from — no wildcards or filters).

from.description: Id of the node whose evidence decides.

path.description: A $.dotted path into that evidence, e.g. "$.verdict".

cases.description: choice: the outgoing arms, tried in order. Exactly one is taken. `when` values must be unique.

when.description: The value that selects this arm (compared to on.path's value).

next.description: Sibling id to enter, or the implicit terminal done/failed.

default.description: choice: where to go when no case matches. Omit to make an unmatched value a HARD ERROR (the run halts) rather than a silent fall-through.

label.description: Human-readable label for the PR status comment / phase label (defaults to a humanized id).

next.description: Id of the sibling node to enter after this one completes. Omit on a terminal node; the terminals 'done' and 'failed' are implicit and need not be declared.

workflow.description: agent: the gh-aw agent workflow basename the engine dispatches, as '<name>.lock.yml'. code (dispatched mode): a plain hand-written GitHub Actions workflow basename, dispatched as '<name>.yml' -- the peer of 'script' (inline mode). Exactly one of 'script'/'workflow' is required on a code node.

evidence.description: agent/code(workflow): the *.evidence.schema.json filename (in the protocol dir) the agent, or the dispatched workflow's uploaded artifact, must satisfy.

max_iterations.description: agent/code(workflow): max iterate-with-feedback rounds before the node is marked failed (default 3).

params.description: agent/code(workflow): node-scoped config forwarded to checks via the CHECK_PARAMS env var (e.g. the rubric categories).

checks.description: agent/question/code(workflow): deterministic checks run over the evidence.

conclude.description: agent ONLY: a trusted (zone 4) hook whose sole job is to read the evidence and decide the node's exit code. Nonzero = the step objects (red check-run); stdout (optional) becomes the check-run summary. 'blocked' is not part of its ABI. FORBIDDEN on a dispatched code node (workflow:) -- a dispatched job has a real exit code, which IS its verdict; a conclude hook would be a second, incoherent verdict source for the same node.

on_blocked.description: agent/code: whether this node's objecting also stops the run -- a nonzero 'conclude' exit, a failed 'on_fail: "block"' check (no hook involved), or a nonzero code hook exit. 'halt' stops the pipeline (overridable via /override); omitted, a red node keeps flowing.

inputs.description: agent/approval/question/code: earlier nodes' outputs to materialize for this node.

states.description: sequence: the grouped steps, a nested sequence of full nodes. The group is entered as ONE unit: what follows it follows the whole group, not its last child.

branches.description: fork (static): the parallel legs. Each leg is an ordinary node with a declared 'kind' — agent, code, or sequence. Exactly one of 'branches' or 'expand'+'each' must be set.

expand.description: fork (dynamic): a trusted hook that expands into per-leg items. Exactly one of 'branches' or 'expand'+'each' must be set.

hook.description: Expander id. Resolved to expand/<hook> or expand/<hook>.* in the protocol dir (extension-agnostic) unless 'exec' is given.

exec.description: Explicit path (relative to the protocol dir) to the expander executable, overriding the expand/<hook> lookup.

as.description: Alias each expanded item is materialized/staged under for its leg.

id_from.description: JSONPath-ish expression into each item selecting the value the leg id/key is derived from.

max_legs.description: Hard cap on expanded legs; the expander fails loud if the item count exceeds it.

matrix_fields.description: Optional: which item keys are inlined into matrix.leg.inputs for the agent. Unset = the full item. The full item is always persisted on the state branch; this only trims what rides the GHA matrix (large re-fetchable fields stay out).

each.description: fork (dynamic): the leg template applied per expanded item — a flat leg (workflow) XOR a sub-pipeline (states), like a 'branch' without 'id'.

of.description: join: the id of the sibling fork this join is an AND-barrier for.

questions_from.description: question: names the sibling node whose evidence carries the questions to ask (answered via the command's /answer prefix).

channel.description: question: where to ask. 'comment' (default) posts on the PR; 'issue' opens a dedicated GitHub issue (for ref/UI-keyed runs with no PR) and routes the answer back via a marker in the issue body.

approve_excludes_author.description: approval: if true, the PR author cannot approve their own request.

env.description: code (inline/script ONLY): environment variables to forward to the hook, BEYOND the least-privilege baseline (PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, PR, ENGINE_LOCAL, GITHUB_REPOSITORY). Name each secret the hook genuinely needs, e.g. ["PUBLISH_TOKEN"]; anything not listed is not forwarded. FORBIDDEN on a dispatched code node (workflow:) -- the dispatched workflow declares its own secrets via its own 'permissions:'/'secrets:' blocks; 'env' would forward a secret to an inline subprocess that does not exist here.

script.description: code (INLINE mode): the task body — the trusted (zone 4) script this node runs, resolved to scripts/<script> or scripts/<script>.* in the protocol dir (extension-agnostic). The peer of the dispatched mode's 'workflow'. Named a 'reduce' script when the node reduces a fork's legs via inputs[].from_fork, but a code node needs no fork — it may run any deterministic step. Exactly one of 'script'/'workflow' is required on a code node.

then._comment: Exactly one of `script` (inline mode, the task body) or `workflow` (dispatched mode, a plain GitHub Actions workflow basename) is required — the two execution modes of a BPMN Script Task. `inputs` was mandatory when this kind was named `merge` and meant 'reduce the joined legs' — a code node with nothing to reduce was incoherent. As a general BPMN Script Task it is not: 'a protocol whose only step is a code script runs to done with no agent' needs no inputs at all. Requiring it forced authors to write `"inputs": []` to satisfy a validator, and made the reference's own `sequence` example fail the linter that same page tells you to run. NOTE (asymmetry, deliberate): this arm cannot ALSO express 'conclude is illegal only when workflow is present', or 'evidence/checks/params are illegal only when script is present', cleanly alongside additionalProperties:false without duplicating the whole property map above. Those four rules (conclude+workflow, env+workflow, evidence/checks/params+script) live ONLY in lib.validate_protocol (the semantic layer, which always runs and gives a better message naming the node id) — see tests/engine/test_dispatched_code_validation.py. Do not 'fix' this by trying to inline them here.
